issues.issue: Were the Member's findings on the likely length of detention speculative, given the PRRA time estimate?
issues.applicant_position: Member speculated about PRRA duration; detention should have continued until the Minister's time estimate ran out.
issues.respondent_position: Minister gave no clear PRRA timeline; the Member's uncertainty concern had an evidentiary basis.
issues.result_quote: I do not agree that this part of the decision amounts to speculation.

issues.issue: Was the finding that the respondent is unlikely to report on imminent removal inconsistent with the section 244 detention rule?
issues.applicant_position: Finding that he is unlikely to report on imminent removal contradicts section 244, which requires continued detention.
issues.result_quote: I do not agree that the passage relied upon by the Minister can be read in isolation from Member McPhelan’s remaining analysis.

issues.issue: Was release on bond, surety and conditions unreasonable, as a departure from earlier findings without clear reasons?
issues.applicant_position: Given lack of credibility and key role in the smuggling, anything short of detention was perverse and an unexplained departure.
issues.result_quote: This argument is no more than an invitation to reweigh the evidence and that is not the role of the Court on judicial review.

issues.issue: Was the bondsperson finding inconsistent with the finding that the respondent was unlikely to care about the surety's finances?
issues.applicant_position: Finding he would not care about the surety's money is inconsistent with finding her an acceptable bondsperson.
issues.result_quote: I also do not agree that there is an inconsistency in Member McPhelan’s finding
